subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should OpenClaw treat image/video-output provider model refs as unsupported chat/session models with clear diagnostics, or add a first-class output-modality contract that routes those refs through media generation?
rationale: Both choices change public provider/model semantics: diagnostics need a way to identify output-only models, while first-class support crosses provider contracts, media tools, response handling, and channel delivery.

options.title: Diagnostic-first contract
options.body: Add or derive output-modality metadata only far enough to reject media-output chat/session selections clearly while keeping generation on image_generate and video_generate.

options.title: First-class media-output routing
options.body: Add output modality metadata and route selected image/video-output model refs through media-generation runtime with channel delivery support.

options.title: Wait for plugin proof
options.body: Keep core unchanged until a Poe or generic media provider plugin proves the missing API surface and desired workflow.

recommendation.title: Diagnostic-first contract
recommendation.body: Add or derive output-modality metadata only far enough to reject media-output chat/session selections clearly while keeping generation on image_generate and video_generate.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product/API boundary choice across provider model semantics and media-generation routing rather than a narrow code repair.
